sentences.text:
Applicant, accused in F.I.R. bearing No.61/2013 registered with Oshiwara Police Station, Mumbai for the offences punishable under Sections 406, 420 r/w. 34 of the Indian Penal Code, has filed this application under Section 482 of the Criminal Procedure Code, seeking to quash the said F.I.R.
Jyoti APL-500-2013 Final.doc 2) Heard learned Advocate Mr. Niranjan Mundargi for the Applicant and learned APP Mr.Vinod Chate for Respondent-State.
Perused the Record.
3) Record indicates that, by an Order dated 23 rd March 2017, Rule was granted.
By way of an interim relief, police was directed to continue with the investigation but not to submit the charge-sheet without the leave of this Court.

4) Record further indicates that, notice of hearing was duly served to Respondent No.2, however,
none appears for Respondent No.2 when taken up for final hearing.

5) The impugned F.I.R. came to be registered on the report filed by Mr. Subhash Bhoir on 19th February 2013, wherein he narrated that, in July 2008, Dr. Dulip Bhosale, who is a co-accused with the Applicant met with Respondent No.2 at his residence and informed him that, flats are available at cheaper rates in Dubai.
On purchasing such a flat one gets the residence VISA of Dubai and if said flat is sold after 4-5 years it will give double profit.
Further Dr. Dulip Bhosale informed that, four other doctors have also transacted with him to purchase such a flat.
Thereafter, Dr. Dulip Bhosale telephoned to the Applicant and called him at the house of Respondent No.2.
Accordingly after some time, the Applicant went there and showed to Respondent No.2 the entire papers of the said flat alongwith Jyoti APL-500-2013 Final.doc brochure thereof.

At that time the Applicant informed that,
the price of the said flat would be Rs.40 Lakhs, out of said amount Rs.12 Lakhs was to be paid in the first slot and thereafter the payment receipt and agreement will be given.
The Respondent No.2 accepted that offer, showed his willingness to purchase the flat and requested some time to pay the said amount of Rs.12 Lakhs.

On the very next date the Applicant and Dr. Bhosale telephoned to Respondent No.2 for inquiring about the initial payment of Rs.12 Lakhs.
6)
On 29th July 2008, the Applicant and co-accused called Respondent No.2 at Rhythm Restaurant and Bar alongwith the money.
In turn Respondent No.2 alongwith his friend Mr. Omprakash Bhatia went to the said Bar carrying amount of Rs.12 Lakhs.
The Applicant and co-accused Dr. Bhosale were present there.
The Respondent No.2 gave Rs.12 Lakhs to the Applicant through Dr. Bhosale.

On inquiry, the Applicant told that, the payment receipt will be sent by the Developer Company,
later on.
Thereafter, the Applicant sent three payment receipts to Respondent No.2, through co-accused Dr. Bhosale.
The two receipts were dated 3 rd August 2008 and one was dated 7th October 2008 for 10,000 Dirhams, 23,750 Dirhams, and 33,750 Dirhams respectively.
Thereafter on continuous follow up through Dr. Bhosale the Applicant bought a Flat Booking Agreement to Respondent No.2, obtained his signature and took it back.
Jyoti APL-500-2013 Final.doc 7)

On further inquiry the accused persons told that, when the main sale-purchase-agreement would be prepared and signed by Respondent No.2, it will be registered at Dubai and given to Respondent Punit S/O Vijaykumar Madhok vs The State Of Maharashtra And Anr on 12 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/151015645/
2 No.2.

sentences.text: Thereafter, the Applicant and co-accused Bhosale brought blank agreement and obtained signatures of Respondent No.2 thereon, with a promise that, after its registration it will be given back to Respondent No.2.
Respondent No.2 inquired about construction project, however he came to know that, there was no such construction and thus he realized that he has been cheated.
8) During further inquiry the Respondent No.2 learnt that, the proposed building is not at Dubai but it is located at Ajman about 200 Kms. from Dubai and there is no building in existence.

When Respondent No.2 inquired with Applicant and co-accused Dr. Bhosale, they told him that due to recession in Dubai no construction will be possible and Respondent No.2 will be given a flat elsewhere.
Thereafter Dr. Bhosale avoided to return the earnest money of Rs.12 Lakhs to Respondent No.2.
Further Respondent No.2 learnt that like him 3 to 4 other persons were cheated by the Applicant.

Hence Police registered this crime against the Applicant and co- accused Dr.
Bhosale.

9) Learned counsel for the Applicant submitted that, there is no material to show that, since inception, there was intention on the part of Jyoti APL-500-2013 Final.doc the Applicant to cheat Respondent No.2 by practicing the fraud upon him, as alleged.
Like Respondent No.2, the Applicant also invested his money in the said project and thus he is also a victim of the same circumstances.

While granting the Anticipatory Bail to the Applicant in Application No. 337 of 2013, this Court has observed that, till then the Investigation Officer did not filed any criminality on the part of the Applicant to attract this offence against him.
Further, he submitted that, in the said Order this Court observed that, the present case is purely of the civil nature.
In the backdrop, the registration of impugned F.I.R. is a illegal and continuation of the same would be abuse of process of law.

Hence,
the said FIR be quashed qua the Applicant.

10) Learned APP submitted that, there is sufficient material against the Applicant that, he has committed the alleged offence by sharing common intention with co-accused Dr. Bhosale, hence the Application be disposed off.
11) In view of the rival submissions we have carefully considered the record.

Admittedly,
Respondent No.2 had paid total Rs.12 lakhs in cash.
In the F.I.R. it is clearly recorded that, the said amount was given by Respondent No.2 to the Applicant through Dr.Dulip Bhosale.
However, the Applicant has not explained as to when he paid that money to the original vendor.
Further, the Applicant has not explained as to when he converted Jyoti APL-500-2013 Final.doc the Indian currency notes in the Dirhams to pay said vendor.
The F.I.R. clearly mentions that no construction activity came up when the Applicant inquired about the said construction project.
Similarly despite promise by the Applicant he did not provide the appropriate Agreement of Sale to the Respondent No.2.
According to the prosecution like Respondent No.2 other three-four persons were also cheated by the Applicant and co-accused with him.
However, the Applicant has not explained as to how he paid amount received from those victims to the vendor and when he converted the Indian Currency notes into Dirhams for the said purpose.

12) No doubt there is a delay in lodging the F.I.R. however the F.I.R. clearly indicates that, when the Respondent No.2 demanded his money back the Applicant was giving evasive replies and he even Punit S/O Vijaykumar Madhok vs The State Of Maharashtra And Anr on 12 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/151015645/
3 avoided to receive his phone calls.

sentences.text: Thus, it seems that some time has been consumed by the Respondent No.2 to recover his money by following with the Applicant.

According to us delay has been reasonably explained by the Respondent No.2.
13) In view thereof, there is a prima facie case against the Applicant of having committed the alleged offence.
13.1) As a result the Application is liable to be dismissed and is accordingly dismissed.

(SHYAM C. CHANDAK, J.) (A. S. GADKARI, J.)
